skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("table.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("table.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use super::{
15.     PteWord,
16.     PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2,
17. };
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Table Entry Trait
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. ///
24. /// # Description
25. ///
26. /// Trait bound for entry types that can be stored in a page table.
27. ///
28. /// The raw representation uses [`PteWord`] — `u32` on x86.
29. ///
30. #[verus_verify]
31. pub trait TableEntry: Copy {
32.     /// Creates from a raw [`PteWord`], returning `None` if the value is invalid.
33.     fn from_raw(raw: PteWord) -> Option<Self>;
34.     /// Returns the raw [`PteWord`] representation.
35.     fn raw(self) -> PteWord;
36. }
37. 
38. //==================================================================================================
39. // Table Index
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. ///
43. /// # Description
44. ///
45. /// A validated index into a page table, guaranteed to be in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`.
46. ///
47. #[verus_verify]
48. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
49. pub struct TableIndex(usize);
50. 
51. #[verus_verify]
52. impl TableIndex {
53.     ///
54.     /// # Description
55.     ///
56.     /// Creates a [`TableIndex`] from a raw `usize`, returning `None` if the value is out of
57.     /// bounds.
58.     ///
59.     #[verus_spec(result =>
60.         ensures
61.             match result {
62.                 Some(t) => index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH && t@ == index as nat,
63.                 None => index >= crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
64.             },
65.     )]
66.     pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Option<Self> {
67.         if index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH {
68.             Some(Self(index))
69.         } else {
70.             None
71.         }
72.     }
73. 
74.     ///
75.     /// # Description
76.     ///
77.     /// Returns the underlying index value.
78.     ///
79.     #[verus_spec(result =>
80.         ensures
81.             result as nat == self@,
82.             result < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
83.     )]
84.     pub const fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
85.         proof! { use_type_invariant(self); }
86.         self.0
87.     }
88. }
89. 
90. //==================================================================================================
91. // Virtual Address Index Extraction
92. //==================================================================================================
93. 
94. /// Extracts the PD index (bits 22-31) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
95. #[verus_spec(result =>
96.     ensures
97.         result@ == spec_pd_index(vaddr),
98.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
99. )]
100. pub const fn pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
101.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
102.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
103.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
104.     proof! {
105.         assert(crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT == 22) by (compute);
106.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
107.             requires index == (vaddr >> 22usize) & 1023usize;
108.     }
109.     TableIndex(index)
110. }
111. 
112. /// Extracts the PT index (bits 12-21) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
113. #[verus_spec(result =>
114.     ensures
115.         result@ == spec_pt_index(vaddr),
116.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
117. )]
118. pub const fn pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
119.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
120.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
121.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
122.     proof! {
123.         assert(crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT == 12) by (compute);
124.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
125.             requires index == (vaddr >> 12usize) & 1023usize;
126.     }
127.     TableIndex(index)
128. }
129. 
130. //==================================================================================================
131. // Table
132. //==================================================================================================
133. 
134. ///
135. /// # Description
136. ///
137. /// A page-table page containing [`PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`](crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH) entries.
138. ///
139. /// This type is parameterized over the entry type to enforce that each table level uses only
140. /// its own entry kind (e.g., PD tables only [`PageDirectoryEntry`], PT tables only
141. /// [`PageTableEntry`]).
142. ///
143. /// The table is accessed via a base address that must be valid in the current address space
144. /// (i.e., a mapped virtual address). It does not own the backing memory — the caller is
145. /// responsible for allocation and lifetime management.
146. ///
147. #[verus_verify]
148. #[derive(Debug)]
149. pub struct Table<E: TableEntry> {
150.     /// Base address of the table (must be page-aligned).
151.     base: usize,
152.     /// Phantom marker for the entry type.
153.     _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData<E>,
154. }
155. 
156. #[verus_verify]
157. impl<E: TableEntry> Table<E> {
158.     ///
159.     /// # Description
160.     ///
161.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
162.     ///
163.     /// # Safety
164.     ///
165.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
166.     /// memory.
167.     ///
168.     #[verus_spec(result =>
169.         ensures result@.addr == base as nat,
170.     )]
171.     pub const unsafe fn from_address(base: usize) -> Self {
172.         Self {
173.             base,
174.             _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData,
175.         }
176.     }
177. 
178.     ///
179.     /// # Description
180.     ///
181.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
182.     ///
183.     /// Returns `None` if the raw value is invalid according to `E::from_raw()`.
184.     ///
185.     /// # Safety
186.     ///
187.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile read.
188.     ///
189.     // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/.../tcb-allowed.md` and `verus-unsupported.md`):
190.     // materializes a raw `*const PteWord` from the integer base address (`usize as *const`) and
191.     // performs a volatile load — the hardware page-table access. Verus does not support the
192.     // `usize -> *const T` cast, so the body cannot be verified; this mirrors the
193.     // `bump_allocator::alloc` / `frame::instance` int-to-pointer materialization boundaries.
194.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
195.     pub unsafe fn read(&self, index: TableIndex) -> Option<E> {
196.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
197.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;
198.         E::from_raw(::core::ptr::read_volatile(ptr))
199.     }
200. 
201.     ///
202.     /// # Description
203.     ///
204.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.
205.     ///
206.     /// # Safety
207.     ///
208.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
209.     ///
210.     // Trust boundary (see `tcb-allowed.md` / `verus-unsupported.md`): materializes a raw
211.     // `*mut PteWord` from the integer base address and performs a volatile store — the hardware
212.     // page-table write. The `usize -> *mut T` cast is unsupported by Verus, so the body cannot be
213.     // verified; same int-to-pointer boundary as `read`.
214.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
215.     pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) {
216.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
217.         let ptr: *mut PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *mut PteWord;
218.         ::core::ptr::write_volatile(ptr, entry.raw());
219.     }
220. }
221.
